history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is the Cathedral of St. Peter the Apostle at Pyndengrei, Nongstoin, the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Nongstoin. The parish was established on 12 May 1966 with Fr. Emmanuel Albizuri SDB as the first parish priest, when missionaries extended pastoral institutions into the western zone of what was then Shillong Diocese. Pope Benedict XVI created the Diocese of Nongstoin on 28 January 2006, bifurcated from the Archdiocese of Shillong; Bishop Victor Lyngdoh was ordained on 2 April 2006 and installed on 4 April 2006 as the first bishop (current bishop: Wilbert Marwein). The diocese covers West Khasi Hills, Eastern West Khasi Hills and South West Khasi Hills districts and had 164,334 Catholics in 2020 (about 28.3% of the territory's population). The cathedral parish includes institutions such as St. Peter's schools and the Salesian sisters' community at Nongstoin (started 25 January 1977). CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this is almost certainly the same church as CSV row 689 'St. Peter's Catholic Church' — there is only one Catholic cathedral in Nongstoin; recommend merging or removing one of the two rows.

name: Nongstoin Catholic Church
town_description: Nongstoin is the headquarters town of West Khasi Hills district, Meghalaya (PIN 793119), set in the Khasi Hills with an overwhelmingly Christian population. It is the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Nongstoin (erected January 2006). Nearby attractions include Nongkhnum River Island and Beach, Weinia Falls, Langshiang Falls and Mawthadraishan Peak.
